## 江山时序 · 中国历史交互地图时间轴 v1.5.0 (Chronicles of the Realm v1.5.0)

🌐 **在线体验 (简体中文)**: https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/
🌐 **在线体验 (繁體中文)**: https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?lang=zh-tw
🌐 **Live Interactive Atlas (English)**: https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?lang=en
📚 **历史专题总览 (Topic Guides)**: https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/topics/
📖 **背后的故事 (Author's Story)**: [从历史课本里的插图，到 GitHub 1k star：「江山时序」背后的故事](https://deanchen.me/history/atlas/2026/10/25/jiangshan-map-story.html)

---

### ✨ v1.5.0 七项主要更新 (What's New in v1.5.0)

#### 1. 移动端体验全链路重构与舆图寻址 2.0
- **舆图寻址挑战升级（`#529`, `#546`, `#557`, `#568`, `#583`, `#501`, `#502`）**：入口提至顶栏，改为 **5 轮 / 100 分制平滑计分**，确保每轮落点年份与城邑存续期对齐；新增**宣纸成绩海报分享卡**，并全面重构移动端控件、底部 Dock 操作栏与揭晓镜头框选。
- **移动端搜索与大事记交互闭环（`#561`, `#563`, `#571`, `#572`, `#582`, `#590`）**：重构移动端搜索胶囊，消除输入聚焦抖动、软键盘挤压与弹窗重叠，搜索轮播新增事件始末与多元历史人物入口；移动端事件气泡收拢进底部大事记折叠栏（粗衬线标题 + 精修定位脉冲环），隐藏年份输入框原生微调箭头。

#### 2. 出海自动语言识别、`localStorage` 记忆与多语精修
- **浏览器语言自适应与记忆（`#491`, `#544`）**：无 `?lang=` 参数时按浏览器首选语言自动落点（非中文系统直入英文版、`zh-TW/HK/MO` 落点繁中、爬虫与嵌入页维持简中），手动切换写入 `localStorage` 记忆（优先级 `?lang=` > 本地记忆 > 浏览器首选）；顶栏拆分语言胶囊收拢为紧凑翻译菜单。
- **英文界面与朗读人声优化（`#492`, `#493`, `#494`, `#516`, `#534`）**：解决英文城邑在默认缩放下重叠、统一英文引号与边缘文案、`?lang=en` 在 `<head>` 预载英文字典；语音朗读优先选用 Premium/Enhanced/Siri 与云扬人声。

#### 3. 首屏同步体积大瘦身与国内移动网络专项提速
- **按需懒加载与运行时加速（`#580`, `#573`, `#498`, `#536`, `#481`, `#540`, `#496`）**：将 `atlas_trace.js` 懒拆为 `atlas_person.js` 与 `atlas_genealogy.js`，**首屏同步脚本 gzip 体积降至 349.3 KB**（7 个同步脚本，11 个懒加载包共延后 1,311.3 KB）；直链按朝代分片加载快照、恢复 `app.js` defer 加载守卫、引入运行时 2D 空间网格与快速搜索索引，并支持脚本加载失败重试。
- **国内移动网络专项优化（`#490`, `#499`）**：解耦海外阻塞脚本，大陆时区字体自动路由至 `fonts.loli.net` 镜像，移动端优先加载 97 KB 轻地形后再按需预热高清底图。

#### 4. 山川地理标注体系、设色门禁与自然边界治理
- **山河形胜标注上线（`#576`, `#578`）**：新增 T0 级边界山脉与大河标注，以及战国、十六国、五代地理分界标注，让山川走势与政权割据一目了然。
- **相邻政权 Lab ΔE ≥ 15 色差门禁与河道对齐（`#564`, `#558`, `#560`, `#569`, `#477`, `#479`）**：建立相邻政权 **Lab ΔE ≥ 15** 自动对比度校验并修复 16 处近色撞色；对齐黄河晋陕峡谷及汾/渭汇口真实河道；战国（巴、楚、越）、南北朝、五代、秦南界全面去除现代省界锯齿，改沿自然山川分水岭。

#### 5. 疆域快照扩容至 221 幅（208 → 221，+13 幅关键节点）
- **新增 13 幅关键历史阶段快照**：包含**战国前 223 灭楚 / 前 222 灭燕代** (`#566`)、**西汉前 174 河西** (`#518`)、**三国 220/221/229 三帝建国分期** (`#532`)、**东晋 327 前凉高昌** (`#528`)、**唐 621–624 / 726–755 黑水都督府 / 842 吐蕃崩解** (`#487`, `#524`, `#577`)、**1259 宋蒙** (`#547`)、**元 1351/1356 红巾军** (`#508`)、**明 1409 奴儿干都司**（羁縻政权渲染，`#507`, `#579`）及**清 1755 准噶尔** (`#518`)。
- **全朝代疆域与政权细节校勘（`#511`–`#567`）**：校订前 403 年战国开篇都城与西部邻邦、胡夏关中长安 (420)、祖逖北伐 (317–319)、刘琨并幽州、隗嚣与窦融、袁术与徐州、晚唐淮南与荆南、阿古柏新疆 (1864–1875)、清中叶阿里/帕米尔及高丽/西突厥邻国名称，并清理政权名冗余括号后缀。

#### 6. 新增「刘裕」精修行迹、全朝代大事记因果脉络与史料出处破 30%
- **精修行迹增至 7 组（`#545`）**：新增南朝宋武帝**刘裕**精修行迹（[`?person=liuyu`](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=liuyu)）及 410–418 核心历史事件；历史人物档案增至 **144 位**。
- **大事记因果脉络补全与时间轴修复（`#575`, `#581`, `#584`, `#585`, `#588`, `#591`, `#586`, `#506`, `#515`, `#519`）**：补齐魏文侯变法、547 侯景叛乱、安庆沿革（桐城派与黄梅戏）及汉、三国、南北朝–隋、唐、宋、元、明清民国大事记因果上下文，时间轴大事增至 **544 条**、地标事件增至 **771 条**；消除时间轴 `focusYear` 死步并同步割据政权年号。
- **一手正史出处突破 30%（`#535`, `#538`, `#586`, `#478`, `#480`, `#482`–`#484`, `#309`）**：全图 1,534 条记录中已有 **479 条（31.2%）** 完成正史 / 《资治通鉴》卷次引用（较 v1.4.0 净增 **96 条**，待补基线由 1,113 降至 1,055），并集中订正 20 余处城邑坐标、名胜与史实疏漏。

#### 7. 视觉预览、四语文档与部署架构轻量化
- **文档与预览图全面刷新（`#551`, `#552`, `#497`, `#556`）**：更新 8 张 README 预览图、2 条中英文 Hero 动图、OG 分享卡片、主页 JSON-LD 及简/繁/英/日四语 README；同步动态 SEO 元数据中的快照与大事记计数。
- **专题页部署时构建（`#504`, `#505`, `#537`）**：128 页静态历史专题改为部署时生成，不再将生成 HTML 提交至 Git 仓库，大幅减轻仓库体积。

---

### 🌍 English Release Highlights (v1.5.0)

1. **Mobile UX Overhaul & Locate Quiz 2.0 (`#529`, `#546`, `#557`, `#561`, `#563`, `#568`, `#571`, `#583`, `#590`)**:
   - Promoted Locate Quiz to the top bar with a **5-round / 100-point** smooth scoring system, a **parchment shareable result poster**, and redesigned mobile controls/bottom dock. Rebuilt mobile search (eliminating keyboard squeeze and focus jank), integrated mobile event callouts into the bottom chronicle peek bar, and added storylines & diverse figures to the search showcase rotation.

# Chronicles of the Realm · 江山时序

English · 简体中文 (Chinese) · 繁體中文 (Traditional Chinese) · 日本語 (Japanese)

**An Interactive Historical Atlas of China from the Warring States (403 BCE) to the Present — Scrub Through Time, Trace Ancient Cities, and Walk in the Footsteps of History** [**Play Live Demo (English UI) → https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?lang=en**](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?lang=en) *The story behind it (in Chinese): [From textbook maps to 1k GitHub stars](https://deanchen.me/history/atlas/2026/10/25/jiangshan-map-story.html)*

--- ## Why It's Fun to Explore Have you ever wondered while reading Chinese history or classical poetry: - *"Where exactly on today's map are Jiankang (the Six Dynasties capital), Huangzhou (where Su Dongpo composed the Red Cliffs Rhapsody in exile), Languan Pass in the Qinling Mountains (where Han Yu halted his horse in the snow), or Zhuxianzhen (Yue Fei's northern campaign frontier)?"* - *"How many names did Chang'an hold across two millennia, and what pivotal events unfolded on that soil?"* - *"How did the realm evolve step by step—from the Partition of Jin and the Seven Warring States at the opening of Sima Guang's Zizhi Tongjian (403 BCE), Qin's unification campaigns, Emperor Wu of Han opening the Hexi Corridor, High Tang's Four Garrisons of Anxi, and Yuan's Xuanzhengyuan jurisdiction over Tibet, to Zeng Jize's recovery of Ili (1881 CE) and the 20th-century shift from the 'Begonia Leaf' (秋海棠) map to the 'Rooster' (雄鸡) map?"* **Chronicles of the Realm (`jiangshan-map`)** brings together **2,400+ years** of Chinese history across **18 historical periods** into a single interactive parchment atlas—featuring **200+ multi-stage territorial and prefecture snapshots**, **ancient cities**, **strategic mountain passes**, **poetic and battlefield landmarks**, **chronological milestones**, and **reigning monarchs & imperial eras**. No heavy print atlases required—just drag the timeline and click any city to travel through space and time. --- ### Feature 1: Scrub the Timeline to Watch Realms Rise & Fall, Track Monarchs, and Compare Ancient & Modern Borders - **Multi-Polity Confrontations on a Single Canvas**: From the Seven Warring States (Qin, Chu, Qi, Yan, Zhao, Wei, Han) alongside Zhou, Yue, Ba-Shu, Zhongshan, and Yiqu, to the Three Kingdoms warlords (Yuan Shao, Cao Cao, Liu Bei, Sun Quan, Gongsun's Liaodong), Northern & Southern Dynasties, Five Dynasties & Ten Kingdoms, and Song, Liao, Western Xia, Dali, Jin, and the Mongols—all rendered side-by-side in high-contrast traditional parchment hues. Hover over any polity in the bottom-left legend to highlight its territory, or click to open that polity's profile (lifespan, capitals and a short history) and zoom to its territory. - **Multi-Stage Territorial Evolution & Dashed "Ghost Boundary Diffs"**: At every major territorial milestone—such as Qin's conquest of Ba-Shu (316 BCE), Yan General Qin Kai's expansion into Liaodong (300 BCE), Ma Yuan's bronze pillars in Jiaozhi (43 CE), Sima Yi's campaign in Liaodong (238 CE), Li Jing's conquest of Tuyuhun (635 CE), the Four Garrisons of Anxi & Wang Xuance's campaign in Central India (648 CE), Yuan's Xuanzhengyuan rule over Tibet (1288 CE), Ming's Jiaozhi Province in Annam (1407 CE), the 1881 Treaty of Saint Petersburg recovering Ili, the 1898 foreign leased territories, the 1945 retrocession of Taiwan, and the 1946 transition from the **"Begonia Leaf" (秋海棠)** map to the **"Rooster" (雄鸡)** map—click any milestone or phase dot to switch maps and reveal the previous phase's dashed vermilion **Ghost Boundary Diff** so territorial gains and losses are immediately visible. - **Reigning Monarch on the Timeline**: The bubble above the timeline names the monarch on the throne in the current year (e.g. `100 BCE · Western Han · Emp. Wu`, `630 CE · Tang · Emp. Taizong`, `1700 CE · Qing · Kangxi Emp. (Shengzu)`); the Chinese interface also shows the regnal era year (`唐太宗·贞观四年`). - **Ancient Prefecture Hover Inspection & Modern Province Overlay**: First-level administrative divisions (Commanderies, Circuits, Routes, and Provinces) are rendered with deduplicated **Parchment Casing** borders. Zoom in and hover over any prefecture (e.g., Ming `Yingtian Prefecture` or Three Kingdoms `Jingzhou`) to inspect its jurisdiction and modern provincial equivalents. In the top-right **Layers** menu, `Provinces` (on by default) draws today's provincial boundaries over the historical map, and `Prov. Names` adds their names. - **Dynamic River Courses, Ancient Lakes & Grand Engineering Works**: As you scrub through time, historical shifts of the Yellow River, expanding and shrinking ancient lakes (*Yunmeng Marsh*, *Lop Nur / Puchanghai*), Warring States/Qin/Han/Ming Great Walls, Sui-Tang & Grand Canals, the Silk Road, and Zheng He's maritime routes evolve in lockstep with each era; ancient coastlines around the Bohai Gulf, northern Jiangsu, the Yangtze estuary, and the Pearl River Delta also advance and retreat by era. - **Zoomable, Territory-Only Timeline**: Drag the handles at either end of the timeline inward to zoom into one stretch of history (handy for short eras such as Qin, the Three Kingdoms, or the Five Dynasties); double-click the timeline to return to the full overview. Turn off **Events** in the **Layers** menu and stepping and autoplay stop only at years when territory changes. - **Sources on Milestones**: Select a chronicle milestone and the classical works it rests on appear below it, e.g. 据《后汉书》卷88 (Chinese interface only). - **Voice Narration**: Turn on the narration toggle next to the play button and autoplay reads out each year and its events in the browser's built-in voice; it also follows a person's chronicle on autoplay (requires a browser with speech synthesis). > [Try It Live: Ming Dynasty Yongle 13 (1415 CE) · Two Capitals, Thirteen Provinces & "Yingtian Fu" Inspection →](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=1415&zoom=1.75¢er=115.8,33.2&hover=Yingtian%20Fu&lang=en) ![Ming Dynasty 1415 CE · Yingtian Fu Hover Preview](assets/preview_1415_ming_yingtian_en.webp) --- ### Feature 2: Click Any Ancient City or Strategic Pass to Uncover 2,400 Years of History (`Trace Place`) **Click any ancient city or mountain pass** on the map (or double-click anywhere on the canvas) to open its **Trace Place** genealogy card: - **Bilingual City Lore Banner & 2,400-Year Administrative Genealogy**: At the top of the card, read a curated **poetic epigraph and historical biography** for the city; below, trace how its name and administrative jurisdiction evolved across all 18 historical eras—from Warring States and Qin commanderies, Han regional inspectorates, Tang circuits, and Song routes to Yuan/Ming/Qing provinces and modern municipalities—complete with `Capital` badges and dynastic seat remarks. - **Site-Specific Landmark Events**: Beneath each dynasty row, inspect major historical events that took place right on that spot (e.g., *Shang Yang's Reforms* and *Qin's Unification* at Xianyang, *Guan Yu Flooding the Seven Armies* at Fancheng, the *Xuanwu Gate Incident* at Chang'an, or *Yue Fei's Martyrdom* at Lin'an). Click the **`Chronicles`** pill in the top-right of the card to filter for dynasties with major events, and click any event to time-travel straight to that year! - **Strategic Mountain Passes & Poetic / Battlefield Landmarks**: Explore famous mountain passes—including *Hangu Pass*, *Tongguan*, *Jianmen Pass*, *Yanmen Pass*, *Yumen Pass*, *Yangguan*, and *Shanhai Pass*—rendered with traditional *Hanque* gatehouse icons and strategic terrain notes, alongside famous battlefields and literary landmarks such as *Red Cliffs (Chibi)*, *Gaixia*, *Wuzhang Plains*, *Orchid Pavilion (Lanting)*, *Yueyang Tower*, *Pavilion of Prince Teng*, *Languan Pass*, *Loulan*, *Lop Nur*, and *Issyk-Kul*. > [Try It Live: High Tang Kaiyuan 29 (741 CE) · Open Chang'an's 2,400-Year Genealogy Card →](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=741&place=Chang'an&lang=en) ![High Tang 741 CE · Chang'an Trace Place & Key Events](assets/preview_741_tang_trace_en.webp) --- ### Feature 3: Person Chronicles — Trace Any Historical Figure Across Time & Space Click the top-left **Universal Search Box** (with a rotatable `e.g.` figure preview and quick-search chips, or type any monarch, general, statesman, monk, or poet such as `Cao Cao`, `Huo Qubing`, `Sima Qian`, `Yue Fei`, or `Zheng He`) to open **Person Chronicle (`点人溯事`)**, marking every milestone of their life with numbered pins across changing dynastic borders: - **Zhang Qian's Mission to the Western Regions (138–126 BCE)**: Depart Chang'an, endure over a decade of Xiongnu captivity without surrendering the Han imperial staff, and blaze the trail to Dayuan (Fergana), Kangju, and the Greater Yuezhi. - **Zhuge Liang's Emergence & Northern Expeditions (207–234 CE)**: From the Three Visits at Longzhong and the alliance at Chaisang before Red Cliffs, to entering Shu, the White Emperor City entrustment, the Southern Campaign across the Lu River, Hanzhong's *Memorial on Deploying the Troops*, Mount Qi, and the autumn winds of Wuzhang Plains. - **Liu Yu's Northern Expeditions & Founding of Liu Song (404–422 CE)**: From rising at Jingkou to crush Huan Xuan, storming Guanggu to end Southern Yan, rushing back to defeat Lu Xun, taking Jiangling and dispatching Zhu Lingshi to pacify Shu, to routing Northern Wei with the Crescent-Moon formation, retaking Luoyang and Chang'an, and founding the Southern Dynasties in Jiankang. - **Xuanzang's Pilgrimage to India (627–645 CE)**: Slip past Yumen Pass alone across the Moheyan Desert, scale the icy Bedel Pass, cross the Indus, study at Nalanda Monastery, and debate at Kanyakubja (Kanauj) before returning to Chang'an. - **Li Bai's Grand Travels Across Tang China (701–762 CE)**: From Suyab and boyhood in Shu, sailing out through the Three Gorges at twenty-four, scattering gold in Yangzhou, serving in the Hanlin Academy at Chang'an, meeting Du Fu in Luoyang, receiving amnesty at White Emperor City, to his final years at Dangtu. - **Su Shi's Literary Exile Across Song China (1056–1101 CE)**: From leaving Meishan for the capital Kaifeng and gazing at the moon in Mizhou, to composing the *Red Cliffs Rhapsody* in Huangzhou exile, Huizhou, and crossing the sea to Danzhou on Hainan Island. - **Wang Yangming's Unity of Knowledge & Action (1472–1529 CE)**: From birth in Yuyao and imprisonment in Beijing, to his enlightenment at Longchang in Guizhou, pacifying bandits in Southern Ganzhou, capturing the rebel Prince of Ning in 35 days, teaching at the Tianquan Bridge in Shaoxing, and his final words *"This mind is bright and clear; what more is there to say?"* at Nan'an. - **Multi-Person Chronicles**: Type two or three names into the search box (e.g. `Li Bai, Du Fu, Gao Shi` or `Cao Cao, Liu Bei, Sun Quan`) to merge their journeys onto one timeline in different colors. A co-lifespan ruler marks the years when they were alive at the same time, places where they met in the same year are linked as shared encounters, and the `Shared N` pill narrows the list to just those stops. - **Event Storylines**: Major events unfold stop by stop, just like a person's life, such as Qin's conquest of the six states, the Chu–Han Contention, the An Lushan Rebellion, the Jingkang Catastrophe, and the Long March. The two sides are drawn in different colors, and each side's advances and the changing map follow stop by stop. Each time you step to the next event (`‹ / ›`, `← / →`, or `Space` to auto-play), **the timeline year, reigning monarch, imperial era, and dynastic territories evolve in sync with their footsteps**, highlighting the active transition arc alongside bilingual primary-source excerpts and poems written at that exact site. > [Try It Live: Su Dongpo's Life & Exile Across Song China (1037–1101 CE) →](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?person=sushi&lang=en) ![Person Chronicle · Su Shi's Life & Exile Route](assets/preview_journey_sushi_en.webp) --- ### Feature 4: Easter Egg · Map Pinpoint Challenge — What Imperial Court Rank Would You Earn? Think you know Chinese historical geography? Click **`Quiz`** in the top toolbar (or type `quiz` in the **Universal Search Box** for **`Map Pinpoint · Ancient Place Quiz`**): - **Dynastic Historical Clues + Blind Map Pinpointing**: City labels are hidden while the prompt asks you to locate an ancient city across a 10-round progressive difficulty deck—accompanied by **dynastic historical clues** (without spoiling the modern city name). Drop your pin to preview and adjust, click the **`Confirm ↵`** chip next to the pin to lock in your answer with concentric distance score rings, and earn points based on great-circle distance to the true coordinates! - Complete 10 rounds to receive a traditional imperial cartographic title such as **Grand Historian & Master Cartographer (太史令 · 舆图大家)**, **Director of the Bureau of Operations (职方郎中)**, or **Prefectural Retainer (州郡从事)**. > [Try It Live: Western Han Emperor Wu, Yuanshou 2 (121 BCE) · Start the Map Pinpoint Challenge →](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?year=-121&quiz=locate&lang=en) ![Western Han 121 BCE · Map Pinpoint Challenge Preview](assets/preview_quiz_challenge_en.webp) --- ### Further Reading: Topic Guides Prefer reading to dragging the map? The [**Topic Guides**](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/topics/) (in Chinese) turn the atlas into static pages you can read, search and share: major event storylines, poetic routes and famous battles, territory and administrative changes across the 18 eras, and chronicles of historical figures, cities and passes. Years, places and people on each page jump straight back to the matching view of the map. --- ## Keyboard Shortcuts & Shareable Deep Links ### Keyboard Shortcuts | Key / Action | Effect | | :--- | :--- | | **`/`** or **`Cmd/Ctrl + K`** | Focus the **Universal Search Box**: search **historical figures** (`Qin Shi Huang`/`Zhang Qian`/`Su Shi`), **ancient & modern cities** (`Xianyang`/`Chang'an`/`Luoyang`/`Kaifeng`), **reigning monarchs** (`Emperor Wu of Han`/`Taizong of Tang`/`Liu Che`/`Li Shimin`), **imperial eras** (`Zhenguan`/`Yongle`/`Kangxi`), **poetic & battlefield landmarks** (`Red Cliffs`/`Wuzhang Plains`/`Languan`/`Lanting`), **mountain passes** (`Hangu Pass`/`Jianmen Pass`/`Yumen Pass`), **historical events**, or the **Ancient Place Quiz** | | **`←` / `→`** or bottom **`‹ / ›`** | Jump to the previous / next historical phase, milestone event, or person event stop (hold `Shift + ← / →` to step by `10` years) | | **`Space`** | Auto-play / pause timeline evolution (or auto-advance stops in Person Chronicle mode) | | **`Esc`** | Close active popups/cards, clear search highlights, or exit custom multi-stop routes | | **`Single-click city` / `Double-click map`** | Open the 18-era **Trace Place & Key Events** genealogy card for that location | | **`Hover / Click legend swatch`** | Hover to isolate & highlight that polity's territory; click to open its profile and zoom to its territory | ### Shareable Deep Links Append query parameters to share any historical moment, battle, city genealogy, or multi-stop route: - Models **never need to guess latitude/longitude coordinates**—simply extract two semantic parameters from a poem or historical text, **`year`** and **`place`**, and the atlas automatically resolves ancient/modern place names, centers the camera, renders dynastic borders and multi-stop trajectories, and opens the **Trace Place** genealogy card: - **Machine-Readable Specification**: [`llms.txt`](llms.txt) - **Zero-Dependency Local MCP Server (`stdio`)**: [`scripts/mcp_server.js`](scripts/mcp_server.js) — add to Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, or Gemini CLI `mcpServers`: ```json { "mcpServers": { "jiangshan-atlas": { "command": "node", "args": ["/absolute/path/to/jiangshan-map/scripts/mcp_server.js"] } } } ``` Exposes 3 native MCP tools (`<5ms` offline response, zero npm dependencies): - `inspect_place({ year, place, lang? })`: Returns reigning monarch/era, controlling regime (`polity`), macro-region (`dao/lu/province`), prefecture (`jun/zhou/fu`), modern province/city, 2,400-year `lore`, and shareable deep-link URL. - `inspect_person({ person, stop?, lang? })`: Returns a historical figure or monarch's biography, chronological geocoded stops across dynasties, and shareable deep-link URL. - `search_atlas({ query, limit?, lang? })`: Searches across all ancient cities, poetic & battlefield landmarks, mountain passes, historical figures, imperial eras, and chronological milestones. - **Ready-to-Use Agent Skill**: [`skills/jiangshan-atlas/SKILL.md`](skills/jiangshan-atlas/SKILL.md) (includes the zero-dependency CLI renderer [`skills/jiangshan-atlas/scripts/jiangshan.py`](skills/jiangshan-atlas/scripts/jiangshan.py)) ```bash # Install into Claude Code / Gemini / Jetski global skills directory: mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills ~/.gemini/config/skills && cp -r skills/jiangshan-atlas ~/.claude/skills/ && cp -r skills/jiangshan-atlas ~/.gemini/config/skills/ ``` ### 1. Browser JavaScript API (`window.atlasAPI`) & In-Browser WebMCP (`navigator.modelContext`) In browser automation environments (Playwright) or WebMCP-enabled AI browsers (`navigator.modelContext`), the page automatically registers `jiangshan_locate`, `jiangshan_inspect`, and `jiangshan_open_person`, and exposes `window.atlasAPI`: - `window.atlasAPI.locate({ year, place, zoom? })`: Drives the map to a single location or multi-stop trajectory and returns structured historical-geographic metadata. - `window.atlasAPI.inspect({ year, place, person?, stop? })`: Read-only query returning the controlling polity, ancient prefecture, modern province/city, leg distances, person events, and canonical shareable URL. - `window.atlasAPI.resolvePlace(place, year?)`: Resolves ancient and modern names for cities, strategic passes, poetic landmarks, and battlefields. - `window.atlasAPI.openPerson(person, stop?)` & `window.atlasAPI.search(query)`: Opens a person chronicle on the map or searches across the entire atlas. --- ## Run Locally No dependencies or build steps required. Clone and serve with any static HTTP server: ```bash git clone https://github.com/DeanChensj/jiangshan-map.git cd jiangshan-map python3 -m http.server 8000 ``` Then open `http://localhost:8000` in your browser. Static topic guides under `topics/` are built on deploy; run `node scripts/build_seo_topics.js --html-only` first if you want to browse `/topics/` locally. ## Run with Docker No local dependency needed. Build and start with Docker Compose: ```bash docker compose up -d --build ``` Then open `http://localhost:8008` (the port mapping `8008:80` is set in `docker-compose.yml`). The `Dockerfile` uses a two-stage build: a `node:20-alpine` stage generates the static `topics/*.html` pages, and the final `nginx:alpine` image serves only the runtime static files (`index.html`, `assets/`, `css/`, `js/`, `geojson/`, `topics/`, and metadata files) from `/usr/share/nginx/html`. `.dockerignore` excludes `.git`, `.github`, `docs/`, `skills/`, `workers/`, unused `data/` and `scripts/` subdirectories, Markdown files, `geojson/demo.html`, and README demo images (`assets/hero_demo_*.webp`, `assets/preview_*.webp`). To use another port, change the `ports` mapping in `docker-compose.yml` (e.g. `"9000:80"`) and run `docker compose up -d` again. After pulling upstream changes, rebuild with `docker compose up -d --build`. Without Compose: `docker build -t jiangshan-map:latest .` then `docker run -d -p 8008:80 --name jiangshan-map jiangshan-map:latest`. Note: the image is built locally; it is not published to any registry. --- ## GeoJSON Export (for Leaflet / MapLibre / QGIS) The app ships its geometry as compact topology-deduplicated VLQ bundles. To use the vector layers in other projects, generate standard RFC 7946 GeoJSON (EPSG:4326, lon/lat) locally; the output goes to `geojson/` and is not committed. The export covers 403 BCE to 1948; later years and the modern province layer are not included. The prefecture layer (郡 / 州 / 府) is left out by default because it derives from CHGIS, whose terms forbid redistribution; add `--with-prefectures` to include it for local academic, non-commercial use, and do not publish the result. ```bash node scripts/export_geojson.js # or: node scripts/export_geojson.js node scripts/export_geojson.js --with-prefectures # adds the CHGIS-derived prefecture layer (local academic use only) ``` - `snapshots/.geojson` — one file per territorial phase; each feature has a `bbox` and `layer` (`polity` / `region`, plus `prefecture` with `--with-prefectures`), `title`, `title_en`, `category`, `tint`, `anchor`. - `index.json` — every dynasty's phases with `from` / `to` years (negative = BCE, no year 0) and the matching snapshot file. - `corridors.geojson` (walls, canals, roads, sea routes), `settlements.geojson`, `milestones.geojson`, `neighbors.geojson`, and `modern/` (rivers, lakes, hydro labels; `appear` / `vanish` give the years historical river courses and lakes are shown). To look up a point without loading every phase, use [`geojson/jiangshan-locate.js`](geojson/jiangshan-locate.js): it loads `index.json` plus only the snapshot covering the year, then runs a bbox-filtered point-in-polygon test. ```js const atlas = JiangshanLocate.create(); // or create({ base: '' }) const hit = await atlas.locate(118.78, 32.06, 1415); // lon, lat, year hit.polity.properties.title; // 明 hit.region.properties.title; // 南直隶 hit.prefecture; // null unless exported with --with-prefectures (then 应天府) ``` After exporting, serve the repository (`python3 -m http.server 8000`) and open `http://localhost:8000/geojson/demo.html` for a Leaflet example: drag the year slider, click the map, or open `demo.html?year=1415&lon=118.78&lat=32.06` to load, highlight and zoom automatically. Historical borders are schematic approximations, not surveyed boundaries.
